model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; GAAP earnings ex acquisition charges after regulatory capital retention, deposits and borrowings not net debt, preferred stock deducted at par)

equity_bridge.item: Preferred stock at liquidation preference (Series H/I/J/K/L plus Comerica series assumed)
equity_bridge.note: PreferredStockValue $2,182m at 30 Jun 2026, Q2-2026 10-Q. Deducted at par instead of stripping ~$150m/yr of preferred dividends from the flows; the two are not both applied.

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: For a bank the distributable-earnings series is net income: FY2020 1,427 (COVID provisioning trough, provision 1,148); FY2021 2,770; FY2022 2,446; FY2023 2,349; FY2024 2,314; FY2025 2,522. The 5-year CAGR (12.1%) measures recovery from the FY2020 trough, not trend; the 3-year (1.0%) measures a flat standalone bank with NII squeezed by 2023-24 deposit betas. Revenue (NII + fees, Metrics CSV): FY2020 7,612; FY2022 8,375; FY2025 9,017; FY2026E 12,880 on eleven months of Comerica. All pre-merger CAGRs describe the standalone bank; the combined bank has one full quarter of history (Q2-2026).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average revenue growth after FY2027 (4.0% fading to 2.5%), anchored on the standalone 5-year revenue CAGR (3.4%); FY2027 itself carries a twelfth month of Comerica (+~2pp) on top of organic growth.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (-1.2%) diverges >30% from revenue (3.4%) and EPS (14.1%): book value was hit by the 2022 AOCI mark on the securities book (equity fell 22,210 -> 17,327 in FY2022) and then jumped 59% in Q1-2026 on the all-stock Comerica issuance, so equity CAGR does not describe the earnings power. EPS 5-year CAGR is measured from the FY2020 COVID trough ($1.84). Growth is taken from the revenue series and management's FY2026 guidance.

scenario_narratives.base: Fifth Third integrates Comerica on plan: the $850m synergy target is largely delivered by FY2027 but reinvested in 50+ Southeast and Texas branches a year and technology, so the efficiency ratio settles around 55% rather than the low 50s. Revenue grows 6% in FY2027 on a twelfth month of Comerica and ~3.5% organic, then fades to 2.5%. Credit normalises to ~40bp of loans on a book that is now ~60% commercial. CET1 is rebuilt to the middle of the 10.0-10.5% band in FY2027 and thereafter ~80-85% of earnings is distributed through the $0.42 quarterly dividend and resumed buybacks. At a 10% cost of equity and a high-teens return on tangible equity (the goodwill from a 20%-premium all-stock deal sits outside TCE) the combined bank is worth roughly 2.2x tangible book, which is where the market has it.
scenario_narratives.bull: Comerica's middle-market, specialty commercial and Texas/California footprint compounds faster than the Midwest core, the Southeast de novo programme keeps taking deposit share, and the deposit book reprices down faster than assets so NIM widens. Full synergies plus operating leverage take the efficiency ratio to 52% by FY2029 with credit still benign (~35bp). Earnings reach ~$5.5bn by FY2029 and the bank distributes most of it; a 3% terminal growth rate on a 45% pre-tax margin is worth materially more than today's price.
scenario_narratives.bear: The largest deal in Fifth Third's history slips: systems conversion loses Comerica commercial deposits, synergies arrive late and integration charges run into FY2027. At the same time the 5%+ 10-year that hit regional banks in September 2026 proves durable: deposit costs stay sticky, loan demand stalls, and a 2027-28 credit turn in commercial real estate and leveraged middle-market lending lifts the provision to 8-10% of revenue (60-75bp NCO). Buybacks are suspended for two years while CET1 is rebuilt through retained earnings. Growth settles at 2% and the pre-tax margin recovers only to ~37%, leaving the bank worth roughly 1.8x tangible book, a fifth below today's price.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A super-regional bank is valued on what it can distribute after funding its regulatory capital, discounted at a USD cost of equity, never on statutory operating cash flow (which is loan-sale and deposit movement) and never with deposits or FHLB/senior debt treated as net debt. Earnings ex acquisition charges are the flow, the core-deposit-intangible amortisation is added back because it is book-only, capital retention at the CET1 target is the reinvestment, preferred stock is deducted at par, and 10% is the return an owner requires with the 10-year at 5%. The result is the residual-income answer in FCFE form: at a high-teens return on tangible equity and 2.5% growth the franchise is worth ~2x tangible book, which is roughly what the market pays, so the stock is a fair-value hold rather than a bargain, and the 15% hurdle entry price sits far below the quote.
key_risks_to_valuation: Integration: every 10% of the $850m synergy target not delivered is ~$65m after tax (~1.7% of earnings); customer attrition on the Comerica commercial deposit book would hit NII directly
Credit cycle: every 10bp on the provision (on ~$175bn of loans) is ~$175m pre-tax (~4.5% of earnings); FY2020 provisioning was 15% of revenue versus the 5.5-6% modelled
Net interest margin: 5bp on ~$270bn of interest-earning assets is ~$135m of NII (1% of revenue); the FY2026 NII guide is explicitly conditioned on a September 2026 Fed move
Cost of equity: the 10.0% rate embeds a 5.1% 10-year; at 9.0% the base value is ~$7/share higher, at 11.0% ~$6.5 lower (sensitivity grid)
Capital: CET1 9.93% is below the 10.0-10.5% band; a heavier Basel III endgame or Category III treatment as assets pass $300bn would raise retention above the modelled g x TCE
Share count: the 911m fully diluted count is the 30 Jun 2026 figure plus 4m dilutive awards; the H2-2026 buyback will lower it but the model gives no credit until it is in a filing

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NYSE regular close); 52-week range 40.05-59.50.
data_sources.financials: FITB_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, USD millions, FY2007-FY2025 annual plus quarterly and half-year rows to Q2-2026) exported from FITB.duckdb, with kpis NetInterestIncome, NonInterestIncome, buybacks and cash_taxes; SEC XBRL companyfacts for CIK 0000035527 (10-K filed 2026-02-24, 10-Q filed 2026-05-05 and 2026-08-04) for Goodwill, IntangibleAssetsNetExcludingGoodwill, PreferredStockValue, StockholdersEquity, CommonStockSharesOutstanding, IncrementalCommonSharesAttributableToShareBasedPaymentArrangements, ProvisionForLoanLeaseAndOtherLosses, NoninterestExpense, IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit, DividendsPreferredStock, ShareBasedCompensation, PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock, Deposits, LongTermDebt, ShortTermBorrowings and the FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsAmortizationExpense schedule. No filing text is extracted for this ticker (US XBRL route).
data_sources.qualitative: FITB_Analysis.json (2026-09-28): Comerica merger terms and synergy target, FY2026 guidance raised at Q2-2026 (NII, fees, expense, NCO, CET1 target), NYSE listing transfer 12 Jun 2026, September 2026 regional-bank sell-off and analyst target cuts, bull/bear cases.

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E total revenue = net interest income + noninterest income at the midpoints of the raised July-2026 guidance (NII $8.74-8.80bn, noninterest income $4.06-4.16bn; FITB_Analysis.json guidance block). FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026 and carries eleven months of Comerica (closed 1 Feb 2026). H1-2026 actual was 6,103 (NII 4,149 + fees 1,954, SEC XBRL InterestIncomeExpenseNet / NoninterestIncome, 10-Q filed 2026-08-04); Q2-2026 alone was 3,274, an annualised 13.1bn. FY2025 standalone was 9,017. Using FY2026E as FY0 puts year 1 = FY2027 one period from the valuation date, which the engine's end-of-year discounting requires.
inputs.share_count_basis: 906.57m common shares outstanding at 30 Jun 2026 (CommonStockSharesOutstanding, Q2-2026 10-Q) plus 4m incremental dilutive share-based awards (IncrementalCommonSharesAttributableToShareBasedPaymentArrangements, Q2-2026) = 910.6m, rounded to 911m. Q2-2026 diluted weighted average was 915.96m because the Comerica issuance (~245m shares at 1.8663x, 1 Feb 2026) was in the count for the whole quarter while H2 buybacks had not started. Held FLAT: share-based compensation is expensed in the flows, and management's H2-2026 buyback resumption is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat, not an additional credit.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. Deposits ($234.1bn at 30 Jun 2026), long-term debt ($17.6bn) and short-term borrowings ($4.6bn; total_debt above is the sum, recorded for audit only) are operating funding of an OCC/Fed-regulated bank whose cost is already inside net interest income; cash and interest-bearing deposits with banks are held against that funding and are not surplus. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (earnings less capital retained to fund risk-weighted-asset growth at the CET1 target) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. Preferred stock is the one claim that does rank ahead of common and is not inside NII: it is deducted at liquidation preference through equity_bridge.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE before preferred = earnings ex acquisition charges ~3,870 (12,880 x (41.8% - 1.55% SBC - 1.75% CDI amortisation) x (1 - 22%)) + CDI amortisation add-back ~225 - capital retained ~1,375 (CET1 catch-up from 9.93% to ~10.25% on ~$216bn RWA ~540 + organic RWA growth ~4% x tangible common equity 21.1bn ~840). Cross-check on the reported side: H1-2026 GAAP net income 966 after ~$650m pre-tax of Q1 acquisition charges and the day-1 CECL provision on non-PCD Comerica loans; Q2-2026 adjusted EPS $1.02 x 916m = ~$935m, an annualised ~3,740 to common, ~3,890 before preferred. reported_fcf = FCFE + SBC so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory operating cash flow (FY2025 +4,514; Q1-2026 -1,106; Q2-2026 +2,796) is loan-sale, trading and deposit movement and is meaningless as free cash flow for a bank; free_cash_flow in the Metrics CSV is not used. reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC charge.
inputs.sbc_source: ShareBasedCompensation (cash-flow add-back, SEC XBRL): FY2024 164, FY2025 163, H1-2026 188 of which Q1-2026 145 includes the acceleration of Comerica awards at close. Combined-bank run-rate ~$200m/yr = 1.55% of FY2026E revenue. Awards are net-share settled; the withholding tax outflow is not separately tagged and is immaterial at this scale (SBC is 1.5% of revenue), so the add-back figure is used. Narrow house/street band.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income IS the banking business (NII $8.7bn guided), and no cash is added to equity value (matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction).
inputs.buyback_note: PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock: FY2024 625, FY2025 525, H1-2026 nil (repurchases suspended around the Comerica close). Management guided a resumption of regular quarterly buybacks in H2-2026 as CET1 is managed to 10.0-10.5% (9.93% at 30 Jun 2026). The flat count is a modelling convention funded by the SBC charge in the flows; the capital-retention line (capex_pct_path) already reserves the CET1 catch-up, so what remains after retention is distributable as dividends ($0.42/qtr from Q3-2026, ~$1.5bn/yr) and buybacks.
inputs.book_value_anchor: Total shareholders' equity $34,482m at 30 Jun 2026 (StockholdersEquity) less preferred stock $2,182m (PreferredStockValue) less goodwill $9,990m (Goodwill, up from $4,947m at Dec-25 on the Comerica purchase accounting) less other intangibles $1,253m (IntangibleAssetsNetExcludingGoodwill, almost all Comerica core deposit intangible) = tangible common equity $21,057m = $23.23/share on 906.6m. Pre-deal (31 Dec 2025): TCE 14,938 = $22.59/share. Price/TBV = 2.24x. Adjusted ROTCE 19% in Q2-2026 per management; modelled FY2027 ROTCE ~19% falling toward ~17% as TCE compounds faster than earnings. CET1 9.93% at 30 Jun 2026 vs 10.0-10.5% target (FITB_Analysis.json); RWA implied ~$216bn.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows: 10-year Treasury ~5.1% (late Sept 2026, elevated by the rate scare that took regional banks down that week; FITB_Analysis.json) + beta 1.1 x US equity risk premium 4.5% = 10.0%. Beta 1.1 for a top-10 super-regional with a commercially weighted book. One rate across all three scenarios; integration, credit-cycle and rate risk is charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a premium. A normalised 4.5% risk-free would give 9.5%, worth roughly +$4/share in the base case (see sensitivity grid).
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (branches, offices) are immaterial relative to equity and their cost sits inside noninterest expense and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin. No lease line and no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest. Preferred dividends (~$150m/yr; DividendsPreferredStock FY2025 146, Q2-2026 38) are NOT deducted from the flows; instead the preferred stock is deducted at its $2,182m liquidation preference in equity_bridge, which is the larger (more conservative) of the two treatments (PV of the dividend stream at 10% is ~$1.5bn) and avoids charging the preferred twice.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine (as NAB.AX 2026-09-24, IAG.AX 2026-09-23). SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with retention = g x tangible common equity is the clean-surplus equivalent (FCFE = NI x (1 - g/ROTE)) and it goes through the validated slider engine, which also produces the workbook. Engine mapping: revenue = NII + noninterest income; ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax income ex acquisition charges (revenue - noninterest expense ex acquisition charges - provision for credit losses) PLUS share-based compensation PLUS core-deposit-intangible amortisation, as % of revenue (FY2026E: 100 - 56.2 efficiency - 4.7 provision + 1.55 SBC + 1.75 CDI = 41.8%; Q2-2026 actual on the same basis 41.7%: pretax 1,036 + ~220 acquisition charges + 45 SBC + 63 CDI = 1,364 / 3,274); sbc_pct_path = 1.55%; da_pct_path = CDI amortisation on the filed schedule (FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsAmortizationExpense: next-12-months 222, year 2 194, year 3 167, year 4 137, year 5 113; Q2-2026 10-Q) as % of revenue, deducted before tax and added back after, so the non-cash charge is not capitalised in perpetuity; capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to fund RWA growth at the CET1 target = g x TCE/revenue (~1.64 x g) plus the FY2027 CET1 catch-up; cash_tax_rate_path = 22% (FY2025 effective 21.5%, Q2-2026 22.7%; cash taxes paid are far lower (FY2025 185 vs 689 expense) because of renewable-energy and LIHTC tax-credit investments whose cost sits in noninterest expense and other assets, so the GAAP rate is the economic rate); wacc = cost of equity 10.0%; net_debt = 0; equity_bridge = -2,182 preferred at par. ONE-OFFS EXCLUDED from FY0: Q1-2026 acquisition-related charges and the day-1 CECL provision on non-PCD Comerica loans (H1-2026 GAAP pre-tax 1,243 vs ~1,900 on the adjusted basis); integration charges continuing into FY2027 are absorbed by starting the base efficiency ratio at 55.5% rather than the ~53-54% the $850m synergy run-rate implies. Residual-income cross-check on tangible book: P/TBV = (ROTE - g)/(CoE - g) = (18 - 2.5)/(10 - 2.5) = 2.07x x $23.23 = ~$48/share, which the engine base should approximate; the market's $52.10 = 2.24x TBV. Price is the NYSE regular close of Friday 25 Sep 2026, not an after-hours print. 30 Jun 2026 is the latest balance sheet; the Q3-2026 10-Q (due early Nov 2026) will be the first to show the resumed buyback and the CET1 path.

bear.growth_rationale: Higher-for-longer rates (10-year at 5.1%) compress NIM as deposit costs stay sticky while loan demand stalls; Comerica customer attrition through the systems conversion offsets the twelfth month of contribution (FY2027 +2% only); a 2027-28 credit downturn in commercial real estate and leveraged middle-market lending keeps loan growth near zero. Revenue grows 0.5-2%.
bear.margin_rationale: Provision at 8% of revenue in FY2027 and 10% in FY2028 (~60-75bp NCO; FY2020 was 15%, FY2009 far worse) with efficiency drifting to 57.5% on synergy slippage, retention spend and integration overruns. FY2027: 100 - 57.5 - 8.0 + 1.55 SBC + 1.7 CDI = 37.8, taken at 36.2 to carry ~$200m of trailing integration charges; FY2028: 100 - 57.5 - 10.0 + 1.55 + 1.45 = 35.5, taken at 34.9. Recovers to provision 6.5% and efficiency 56.5% by year 6: 100 - 56.5 - 6.5 + 1.55 + CDI 0.6 = 39.2, held at 38.7 as CDI runs off with fees recovering 1pp.
bear.capex_rationale: Retention stays well above g x 1.64 in FY2027-29 despite 0.5-2% growth because RWA migration in a downturn consumes capital (risk-weight inflation on downgraded commercial credits) and the CET1 catch-up still has to be funded; buybacks are suspended for two years. Terminal 2% growth retains 3.3% of revenue.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 6.0% = a twelfth month of Comerica (~+2.3pp on a ~$3.5bn/yr acquired revenue base) plus ~3.5% organic (loan growth ~3-4%, NIM roughly flat as deposit repricing offsets asset-yield drift, fee growth mid-single-digit from wealth and treasury management). Then 4.0% tapering to 2.5% terminal (nominal GDP less structural NIM compression), in line with the standalone 3.4% 5-year revenue CAGR plus the Southeast/Sun Belt de novo programme (50+ branches/yr to 2028).
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax ex acquisition charges + SBC + CDI amortisation, on revenue. FY2027 42.7% = 100 - efficiency 55.5% - provision 5.5% + SBC 1.55 + CDI 1.65 (rounded). Efficiency held at 55-55.5% (FY2026E guide 56.2%, Q2-2026 57%): the remaining Comerica synergies are offset by trailing integration charges in FY2027, 50+ new branches a year and technology spend. Provision 5.5% of revenue (~40bp of ~$175bn loans) rising to 6.0% mature (~43bp): FY2019 5.6%, FY2024 6.3%, FY2025 7.3%, guided 30-40bp NCO for FY2026; the model does not assume Q2-2026's 129 (1.6% annualised) repeats. Mature: 100 - 55.0 - 6.0 + 1.55 + CDI as it runs off = ~40.6.
base.da_rationale: Core deposit intangible amortisation on the filed schedule (222 / 194 / 167 / 137 / 113 for the next five years, Q2-2026 10-Q) over projected revenue, running off to ~0.1% by year 10. Non-cash, book-only (an all-stock reorganisation carries no tax step-up), added back after tax; the ~$50m/yr tax shield the engine implies on the deduction is the only simplification and is inside the 22% rate's rounding.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold CET1 in the 10.0-10.5% band as RWA grows with revenue = g x TCE / revenue = ~1.64 x g (TCE 21.1bn on FY2026E revenue 12.9bn). FY2027 10.0% (~$1.37bn) = 4% organic RWA growth (~$840m; the extra Comerica month needs no new capital, it is already on the balance sheet) plus a ~$540m catch-up from 9.93% to ~10.25% CET1 on ~$216bn RWA. Thereafter 6.5% at 4% growth falling to 4.1% at 2.5% terminal growth, i.e. ~85% of earnings distributable at maturity (dividend ~$1.5bn/yr plus buybacks), consistent with management's stated intent to return capital above the CET1 target.

bull.growth_rationale: Comerica's middle-market and specialty commercial franchise and the Southeast/Texas branch build compound loans at 5-6% with NIM widening as the deposit book reprices down faster than assets; wealth fees grow high-single-digit on ~$690bn assets under care. Revenue +8% FY2027 (twelfth Comerica month plus ~5.5% organic) fading to 3% terminal.
bull.margin_rationale: Efficiency ratio reaches 52% by FY2029 (full $850m synergies plus operating leverage on a larger base; Q2-2026 already 57%) and credit stays benign at ~5% of revenue (~35bp): 100 - 52 - 5 + 1.55 + CDI. Held at ~45.5 as CDI runs off.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = g x TCE/revenue at ~1.64x: faster growth needs more capital even at a higher return. FY2027 includes the same ~$540m CET1 catch-up. Terminal 3% growth retains ~4.9% of revenue (~15% of earnings).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25%: the Comerica integration is the largest in the company's history and has one quarter of combined results behind it, CET1 sits below the target band while buybacks are about to resume, and the September 2026 rate scare (10-year ~5.1%) is exactly the macro that turns a benign credit book. Bull cut to 25%: it needs the synergy overshoot, NIM expansion, Sun Belt share gains and benign credit all to hold for a decade, and at 2.24x tangible book the market already prices a high-teens ROTCE.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
